Six Flags is pretty much mostly thrill seeking rides/different types of roller coasters. Disneyland is fun for everyone (except for the long lines) because its themed around Disney...but there will be also more fat people and kids, and the rides are supposed to be mild enough for most kids, but the rides themselves are entertaining (though less thrilling). Universal Studios is less trill seeking and the rides are more about experience (eg virtual reality rides, driving through "Jurassic Park" with a drop at the end, etc...I think there is a new Hogwarts area too). The differences between theme parks are a lot so I couldn't really recommend any. It depends more on what you want to experience the most.

If you're thinking of traveling through CA, look up the Amtrak train. It runs the length of CA and can get you to any of the major CA cities. There's also the greyhound bus but travel time takes longer. Renting a car is also a good idea if you want more independence, but getting from one major point to another could take anywhere between 1-6 hours driving. CA could be its own country, it's pretty big for its own state.

You have to stow your bags in a storage area that is accessible to anyone, so I would just sit somewhere where you can see the storage area and watch your luggage. If your luggage is small enough you can try to shove it under your seat, but if the train gets crowded people get asked to move their luggage to the luggage racks. Overall Amtrak/train would be more comfortable than a bus. Bus I would chose as a last resort if there is a specific place you need to get to, that the bus is closer to than the train.
